scripts.title: 32Bit Base Relative Writes
scripts.documentation:
# 32Bit Base Relative Writes

This code accepts 32bit values as an input, then writes them to a specified offset to the base address.

To find the base offset of specific addresses, you can use the [Big Gen 4 Memory Map][RAM_MAP]. Enter the desired offset into the "offset" variable. Please note that all 32-bit writes are word-aligned, so offsets should always be numbers divisible by 4.

The value to be written should be entered into the "value" variable.

## 16Bit and 8Bit writes

To modify this code to apply 16Bit or 8Bit base relative writes instead, modify the "str r2, [r0, r1]" instruction on line 4 of the assembly script.

- For 16Bit writes, modify it to "strh r2, [r0, r1]". All writes will now be halfword aligned, so the offset variable should be even.
- For 8Bit writes, modify it to "strb r2, [r0, r1]". All writes will now be arbitrary, so the offset variable can be any value.

## Technical details

The first LoadAdrsValue command alters the CmpRegReg command. When CmpRegReg (command 0x000B) is executed, the game will now instead branch and exchange to the address of the first CmpRegReg argument, contained in register r0. Since this argument is set up at uneven address, this causes execution in Thumb. 

The following assembly code then adds an offset to the base-relative address stored in r0, writing the desired value to a new base-relative address.

To ensure a safe return, a pop {r4, pc} instruction needs to be used, to match the push {r4, lr} instruction used at the start of the command.

[RAM_MAP]: https://docs.google.com/document/d/13PyrVMX0YW8HjUHeXUgpRkmTJDnzjFDHWuqeMeMGUMk/edit?tab=t.0

code.assembly:
code:
add r0, #0x9                    @ r0 now points to the start of data
ldmia r0!, {r1, r2}
str r2, [r0, r1]                @ r0 + r1 points to target address
pop {r4, pc}

data:
.word [offset] - 0x13A4         @ r0 points to base + 0x13A4 after ldmia, so take that into account
.word [value]
